headline: Group agreed to shorten its mission statement, to form a strategic planning subcommittee, and to hold a potluck brunch in December.

plain_text:
1 | P a g e  
 
City of Nashua 
Division of Public Health and Community Services 
 
Mayor’s Task Force on Substance Misuse Meeting 
 
Tuesday, 11/17/2026 
9:30 – 11 a.m. 
Facilitator: Bobbie Bagley, Director DPHCS         Location: City Hall Auditorium, 3rd Floor 
Minutes 
Mission Statement  
• The mission for Mayor’s task Force on Substance Misuse was read and 
discussed. 
• The group agreed that the mission statement should be shortened. Several 
changes were discussed and made. 
• The revised mission statement will be shared with the group for additional 
feedback and suggestions. 
• The group emphasized that its approach should be data-driven and evidence-
informed to guide decision-making. 
• Behavioral health and mental health should also be incorporated into the 
mission statement. 
SSANA Update 
• October was the first full month operating from the parking lot. The change in 
location may have affected participation, as some individuals may not be 
aware of the new location or may feel uncomfortable accessing services there. 
The team is exploring privately owned parking lots for potential locations. A 
few leads have been identified, but none are ready yet. 
• There was a 27% decrease in individuals served compared to October of last 
year. 
• There have been 2,947 transactions year-to-date, reflecting an overall increase 
in transactions. 
• The program reported more overdose reversals and increased street outreach 
encounters compared to last year. 
• The current syringe return rate is 90%. The state requires a 95% return rate. 
• The group discussed concerns about individuals leaving belongings behind 
when relocating and later returning to request additional supplies. United Way 
continues distributing tents and stay-warm bags. 
• No other agencies are distributing syringes, although individuals can purchase 
them independently. Concerns were also raised about discarded syringes in 
public areas. 
• A comparison of SSANA transactions in 2025 and 2026 was presented.  
AMR/PD Data 
• Opiate-related overdose deaths increased by 2 from October 2025 to October 
2026 and by 3 year-to-date compared to 2025, with 18 deaths reported during 
the most recent 12-month period.
2 | P a g e  
 
Housing Services 
Officer Update 
• The feasibility study is moving forward, with Phase 1 completed and 
community feedback received. Phase 2 involves incorporating the feedback 
into the architectural design. The Homeless Services Gap Analysis Committee 
is working to identify gaps and unmet needs and develop formal 
recommendations for the Board of Aldermen. The Proof of Concept 
partnership with Harbor Care launched on October 5, and participation 
numbers have been steadily increasing. 
Warming Station Update: 
• The Warming Station opened successfully, with more than 15 individuals 
attending the first night. 
• Expectations and guidelines were explained to guests. 
• The Warming Station operates as a low-barrier program, allowing individuals 
who use substances to access shelter and remain safe from extreme weather. 
• The group discussed the importance of the Warming Station's primary goal: 
preventing deaths. 
• The group discussed establishing clear expectations for guests, particularly 
regarding substance use outside the facility. 
• Staff cannot monitor the outside area, and guests may be informed that they 
cannot return inside if they choose to use substances outside. 
• The group discussed whether substance use outside the facility should be 
addressed differently. 
Discussion/Next 
Steps 
 
• Work on the strategic plan will resume in January. 
• The Prevention Coalition and REVIVE will be contacted to begin developing 
activities focused on youth prevention. 
• A subcommittee will be formed to support the strategic planning process. 
Initial members will include Leah, Jessica, Iraida, Sakshi, Moana, Eileen and 
Bobbie. 
• The revised MOTF mission statement will be shared with the group for 
additional feedback. 
• The group will reach out to Doorways and REVIVE regarding overdose trends in 
the Hispanic and Latino community. 
• Another Resource Center data analysis will be completed and included in next 
month's update. 
• The group decided having a potluck brunch at the December meeting. A 
reminder will be sent prior to the meeting.  
 
   
Next Meeting December 15, 2026
